path.description: MoE wNa16 CUDA kernel (moe_wna16_gemm_kernel): the grid splits K over blockIdx.z (gridDim.z = size_k / BLOCK_SIZE_K). Each block computes the partial dot product of its K slice for up to BLOCK_SIZE_M (token, expert-slot) rows, scales it by the routing weight when mul_topk_weight, rounds it to the activation type with Dtype::float2num and atomicAdds it into output[token_index * size_n + offset_n], a per-(token, expert-slot) row that moe_wna16_gemm zeroes on entry. The K-slice partials of one output element therefore accumulate in arrival order; with three or more slices the stored value depends on block scheduling. Experts of one token write different rows and do not collide. The kernel source is byte-identical to the July pin. What changed is the dispatch: it is now selected only inside dispatch_fused_moe_kernel (renamed from invoke_fused_moe_kernel), which calls should_moe_wna16_use_cuda when the caller passes an int8/int4 wNa16 config with a group size, and only fused_experts_impl and the dots3 vision MoE helper call that function. The wNa16 quantisation methods no longer reach it: the GPTQ and AWQ moe_wna16 methods (MoeWNA16Method.apply, AutoAWQMoEMethod.apply) and compressed-tensors wNa16 MoE (CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod.apply) all build a modular kernel through the WNA16 backend oracle, whose TRITON backend is TritonWNA16Experts and calls invoke_fused_moe_wna16_triton_kernel only, and whose other backends are Marlin, Humming, FlashInfer TRT-LLM, CPU, XPU or emulation. The CUDA kernel is therefore reachable at this sha only from a direct fused_experts call carrying an int4 W4A16 quant config with group size in {32, 64, 128} at M * top_k / num_experts <= 6 (for example tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py::test_fused_moe_wn16, benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --dtype int4_w4a16 and the census kernel probe); the in-tree production fused_experts callers pass fp8 or int8 configs.
